records.name: Germantown Community Broadcasting
records.summary: The community radio station for Germantown, on the air as G-Town Radio at 92.9 (WGGT-LP). It runs local live shows and podcasts, and it hosts artist residencies with public gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Tune in to live shows and podcasts, come to the public gatherings for the current artist residency, or ask the station how to get involved in its programs.

schedule.text: Live shows run in the morning and at midday (for example 8 to 10 am, 10 to 11 am, 11 am to 12 pm, and noon to 1 pm); three artist residency gatherings were announced for August 2026, with more dates to come on the site

cost.text: The site lists no prices for listening, events or membership.

first_step.how: Listen online at gtownradio.com, then email info@gtownradio.com or call 215.609.4301 to ask how to volunteer as a host or producer
first_step.basis: The Get Involved section says 'Volunteer Today' but gives no details on roles or how to start, so the way in is unclear beyond contacting the station.

records.name: Lest We Forget Slavery Museum
records.summary: A museum in Germantown about the history of slavery, with objects such as shackles and bills of sale and panels that explain the period. It also takes a traveling exhibit to schools and community events.
records.what_you_do: Book a tour at least 24 hours ahead, ask for the traveling exhibit for a school, congregation or community event, or join or give to support the museum's preservation work. The site describes no volunteer program.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday 10 am to 4 pm and Sunday noon to 4 pm; tours by appointment booked at least 24 hours ahead. No upcoming events are listed.

cost.text: No admission fee is mentioned on the page. Memberships and donations support the museum.

first_step.how: Book a tour by phone or email at least 24 hours ahead at (215) 205-4324 or info@lwfsm.com, or ask about the traveling exhibit for your school or group
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a clear way to book; tours are by appointment only, so there are no walk-ins.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a September 27, 2016 audio interview, older than 24 months, so status is dormant. records.name: Network for New Music
records.summary: A Philadelphia new music ensemble that performs contemporary concerts and runs an education program. The program brings workshops to school classrooms, offers residencies to university composers, and runs a paid double bass ensemble.
records.what_you_do: Attend the season's concerts, watch for the open call for double bass players to join the paid ensemble, or donate. School workshops and university residencies are arranged through schools and universities, not by individuals.

schedule.text: Concerts follow a season; the site lists 2025 to 2026 as ended and 2026 to 2027 (Outside the Lines) as upcoming, with no dates on the pages read. The double bass ensemble call for players is open, with no date shown.

locations.label: Batch address (the site shows placeholder text)

cost.text: No concert ticket prices are listed. School workshops are listed at $200 to $500 each, and free for School District of Philadelphia classrooms.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a concert in the season, or email education@networkfornewmusic.org to ask about the next call for double bass players
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public; joining the paid ensemble needs a call and audition, so that route is for players only.

records.notes: Judgment call: the only public routes found are concerts, donations and the paid double bass ensemble, plus school and university programs that individuals cannot sign up for. The brief's ticket-only rule does not quite fit because of the open call for players and the community ensemble language, so the record is publish. A reviewer could reclassify it to not_a_group. The site shows placeholder address and phone text, so the batch address is used. The education page also lists a summer composition period for school musicians with All City Orchestra. The status is probably active because the pages carry a season label but no dated items.

records.name: Wildflower Composers
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs a summer composition festival for young composers aged 13 to 19 who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer. Students take seminars and lessons at Temple University, workshop new pieces with musicians, and hear their work premiered.
records.what_you_do: Apply to the two-week summer festival, where students take seminars and lessons, write a new piece, and work with musicians from Network for New Music. Donors can also support the work. The site lists no volunteer roles.

schedule.text: A two-week summer festival each July on the Temple University campus (the 2026 session was listed for July 6 to 17); online mini-courses and a lab are listed without dates

cost.text: No application fee. Tuition is $900, and dorm room and board add $1,400. Financial aid, including full scholarships, is available.

first_step.how: Apply through the festival's 'Learn more and apply' page, or ask about financial aid before you apply
first_step.basis: The festival needs an application and an eligibility check (students aged 13 to 19 who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer), but the site says no composition experience is required and financial aid is available.

records.notes: The festival page gives July 6 to 17, 2026 and says admissions stay open until filled with three spots left. That does not square with a July session that has already run, so check before sharing. Eligibility per the festival page: students aged 13 to 19 who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer, and able to read music in at least one clef. The homepage describes early-career composers, but the festival page's age range is used. The only email on the site appears to be a person's address, so it is not recorded; use the site's Contact page. Batch alias: Young Women Composers. The office address (22 E Clapier St, 19144) comes from the batch list and is not confirmed on the site.
